<h1 class="csf-hero__title">What to bring when you <em>can't</em> cook</h1>

<p class="csf-hero__lede">
Every dish here feeds 4–6 people, costs a few euro, and needs nothing more than
a bowl, a knife and a fridge. This is the *senza fuochi* part of the name.
</p>
:::

::: {.csf-section}
<p class="csf-section__kicker">Start here</p>
<h2 class="csf-section__title">The absolute minimum</h2>
<p class="csf-section__sub">
If you're reading this an hour before the dinner: buy good bread, a jar of olives,
and a bar of dark chocolate. Total cost about €6. You have contributed. Come anyway.
</p>
:::

::: {.csf-section}
<h2 class="csf-section__title">Nothing to cook at all</h2>

::: {.csf-grid}
::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🍅</span>

### Panzanella
Tear up yesterday's bread, add chopped tomatoes, red onion, basil, plenty of olive oil,
a splash of vinegar and salt. Leave it 20 minutes so the bread softens. Better the
longer it sits, which makes it perfect for carrying across town.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🥕</span>

### Carrot, orange and cumin salad
Grate carrots, squeeze in an orange, add a big pinch of cumin, oil, salt.
Three ingredients, five minutes, and it looks like you tried.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🫘</span>

### Chickpea and tuna salad
Two tins of chickpeas, one of tuna, half a red onion sliced thin, lemon, oil,
parsley. High protein, costs about €3, and it survives a bike ride.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🥣</span>

### Hummus, the lazy version
Blitz a tin of chickpeas with tahini, lemon, garlic and a lot of olive oil.
No blender? Mash it with a fork and call it rustic. Bring carrots and bread to dip.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🧀</span>

### A proper board
Cheese, cured meat or olives, fruit, bread, nuts. Zero cooking. Arrange it on
anything flat. This is always one of the first things to disappear.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🍉</span>

### Watermelon, feta and mint
Cube the watermelon, crumble feta over it, tear in mint, black pepper.
Summer only, gone in four minutes.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.csf-section}
<h2 class="csf-section__title">One hob, one pan</h2>

::: {.csf-grid}
::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🍝</span>

### Pasta al pesto, cold
Boil pasta, drain, rinse under cold water so it doesn't clump, stir through pesto
with a spoonful of the cooking water. Add cherry tomatoes and pine nuts if the
budget stretches. Travels fine, eats fine at room temperature.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🍚</span>

### Rice salad
Boil rice, cool it, then throw in whatever is cheap: tinned corn, olives, tuna,
diced cheese, pickles. Dress with oil and lemon. Infinitely forgiving.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🥔</span>

### Frittata di patate
Boil potatoes, slice them, fry with onion, pour over six beaten eggs, cook slowly,
flip with the help of a plate and some courage. Good hot, good cold, feeds many.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🍲</span>

### Lentil soup
Onion, carrot, celery, a tin of tomatoes, a bag of red lentils, water, salt.
Twenty-five minutes unattended. Cheapest way to feed eight people.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.csf-section}
<h2 class="csf-section__title">Dessert without an oven</h2>

::: {.csf-grid}
::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🍫</span>

### Salame di cioccolato
Crush dry biscuits, melt dark chocolate and butter, mix with a little sugar,
roll into a log in baking paper, fridge for two hours, slice.
No oven, and it looks impressive on the table.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">☕</span>

### Tiramisù, no-bake by definition
Mascarpone, eggs, sugar, coffee, savoiardi, cocoa. It was never baked to begin with.
Make it the night before and don't move it too fast.
:::

::: {.csf-card}
<span class="csf-card__icon">🍓</span>

### Fruit with lemon and sugar
Chop whatever fruit is in season, sugar, lemon juice, thirty minutes in the fridge.
It becomes its own syrup. Costs nothing and everyone takes some.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.csf-section}
<h2 class="csf-section__title">Rules of thumb for potluck cooking</h2>

- **Room temperature is your friend.** Nothing that has to be served piping hot.
- **Cook for 4–6, not for everyone.** With fifteen dishes on the table, portions are small.
- **Bring it in the container you'll carry home.** Nobody wants to redistribute your dish at 1am.
- **Label it if it matters.** Contains nuts, contains pork, vegan — a scrap of paper is enough.
- **One dish is one dish.** You are not hosting. You are contributing.
:::

::: {.csf-band}
## Pick one and come

Genuinely — the chocolate option counts.
